page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-core ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture provisions 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, eliminating noisy-neighbor resource contention across virtual threads. The instance includes 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2 GB per core, coupled with 3,800 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD local instance storage and 30 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core scalability and memory throughput. The system achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance (25,249.0), software compilation with Clang (81,908.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (652.42 GB/sec). Memory subsystem measurements indicate superior cache and bus efficiency, delivering 459.25 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 196.82 GB/sec in large-block write operations. Furthermore, operations demanding rapid key-value processing reach top-tier status, evidenced by 133.11 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web serving throughput.

The physical configuration presents distinct operational tradeoffs. While multi-threaded execution and data processing leverage the full 64-core topology effectively, single-thread compute metrics such as stress-ng single-core (1,706.89) and Geekbench single-core (1,890.0) remain in the middle tier. Software stacks relying on x86-specific vector extensions cannot run without re-compilation or architectural adaptation, as the processor utilizes ARM64 instruction sets with hardware AES cryptography instead of AVX instruction sets.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, c8gd.16xlarge delivers substantial compute and high-density local NVMe storage without requiring external block-storage attachments for scratch space. It is particularly well suited for distributed build clusters, static web serving infrastructure, large in-memory caching layers with local persistence, database operations, and multi-threaded data transformation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gd.16xlarge is a 64-core compute-optimized server based on the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. With 64 dedicated physical cores and no multithreading, it delivers consistent CPU scheduling paired with 128 GB of memory, 30 Gbps baseline networking, and 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded compilation, memory throughput reaching 459.25 GB/sec on uncached reads, and robust performance in Redis operations and static web serving. While single-thread benchmarks remain intermediate and workloads require ARM64 binary compatibility, the dense NVMe footprint and strong parallel compute provide solid cost efficiency for distributed compilation, caching layers, batch processing, and high-throughput web infrastructure.
